scenario:
Six runners — Fabre, Gomez, Holt, Ingram, Jenks, and Kwan — finish a road race in six distinct places, first through sixth, with no ties. The following conditions govern the order in which they finish.
1. Fabre finishes before Gomez.
2. Holt finishes immediately before or immediately after Ingram.
3. Jenks finishes before Holt.
4. Kwan does not finish first or sixth.
5. If Gomez finishes third, then Ingram finishes fifth.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be the order of finishers from first to sixth?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gomez, Fabre, Jenks, Holt, Ingram, Kwan

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fabre, Jenks, Holt, Ingram, Kwan, Gomez

choices.label: C
choices.text: Jenks, Kwan, Fabre, Holt, Gomez, Ingram

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fabre, Holt, Jenks, Ingram, Kwan, Gomez

choices.label: E
choices.text: Jenks, Fabre, Holt, Kwan, Ingram, Kwan

explanations.correct: Fabre(1) before Gomez(6) ✓; Holt(3) immediately before Ingram(4) ✓; Jenks(2) before Holt(3) ✓; Kwan(5) is neither first nor sixth ✓; Gomez is not third, so the conditional is not triggered ✓. All rules satisfied.
explanations.A: Gomez finishes first and Fabre second, violating Rule 1 (Fabre must finish before Gomez).
explanations.B: Correct — all five rules are satisfied.
explanations.C: Holt(4) and Ingram(6) are not adjacent (positions 4 and 6 differ by 2), violating Rule 2.
explanations.D: Jenks(3) finishes after Holt(2), violating Rule 3 (Jenks must finish before Holt). Also Holt(2) and Ingram(4) are not adjacent.
explanations.E: Kwan appears twice; each runner finishes in exactly one place — this is an invalid assignment.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

explanations.correct: Rule 1 requires Fabre before Gomez, and Rule 3 requires Jenks before Holt, and Rule 2 keeps Holt and Ingram adjacent. Kwan is restricted to positions 2–5. Because Gomez must come after Fabre (at minimum Gomez ≥ 2), and the Jenks–Holt–Ingram chain occupies at least three slots before or around Gomez, Kwan (limited to positions 2–5) always lands at a lower position than Gomez who can reach 6. In every valid solution Kwan's position is strictly less than Gomez's position, so Kwan must always finish before Gomez.
explanations.A: Fabre can finish second (e.g., Jenks-1, Fabre-2, Kwan-3, Holt-4, Ingram-5, Gomez-6), so Fabre does not have to finish first.
explanations.B: Fabre can finish before Jenks (e.g., Fabre-1, Jenks-2, Holt-3, Ingram-4, Kwan-5, Gomez-6), so Jenks need not finish before Fabre.
explanations.C: Gomez can finish fourth (e.g., Fabre-1, Kwan-2, Jenks-3, Gomez-4, Holt-5, Ingram-6), so Gomez need not finish sixth.
explanations.D: Correct — Kwan always finishes before Gomez in every valid arrangement.
explanations.E: Rule 2 says Holt and Ingram are adjacent but does not specify which is ahead; Ingram can finish immediately before Holt (e.g., Fabre-1, Kwan-2, Jenks-3, Gomez-4, Ingram-5, Holt-6... but wait, Kwan cannot be 6 and Gomez must be after Fabre — this specific order needs checking). The adjacency rule allows either order, so Ingram need not always finish after Holt.

questions.questionStem: Each of the following could be true EXCEPT:

explanations.correct: Rule 1 requires Fabre to finish before Gomez. If Gomez finished first, there would be no position earlier for Fabre, making this impossible in every valid arrangement.
explanations.A: Fabre can finish second (e.g., Jenks-1, Fabre-2, Kwan-3, Holt-4, Ingram-5, Gomez-6). Could be true.
explanations.B: Kwan can finish second (e.g., Fabre-1, Kwan-2, Jenks-3, Holt-4, Ingram-5, Gomez-6). Could be true.
explanations.C: Jenks can finish third (e.g., Fabre-1, Kwan-2, Jenks-3, Holt-4, Ingram-5, Gomez-6). Could be true.
explanations.D: Holt can finish sixth when Ingram finishes fifth (e.g., Jenks-1, Fabre-2, Gomez-3, Kwan-4, Ingram-5, Holt-6 — but Rule 5 would require Ingram at 5 if Gomez is at 3, which is satisfied here). Could be true.
explanations.E: Cannot be true — Rule 1 requires Fabre before Gomez, so Gomez cannot be first.

questions.questionStem: If Gomez finishes third, then which one of the following must be true?

explanations.correct: Rule 5 directly states: if Gomez finishes third, then Ingram finishes fifth. With Gomez at 3, Rule 5 fires and Ingram is locked to position 5. This must be true.
explanations.A: With Gomez at 3, Fabre must be at 1 or 2. Both are possible (e.g., Jenks-1, Fabre-2, Gomez-3... or Fabre-1, Jenks-2, Gomez-3...), so Fabre need not be first.
explanations.B: Jenks can be first or second when Gomez is third (see explanation for A), so Jenks need not be second.
explanations.C: With Ingram forced to position 5 (Rule 5) and Holt adjacent to Ingram (Rule 2), Holt must be at 4 or 6. Holt at 6 is one possibility, but Holt at 4 is another; it is not forced to sixth.
explanations.D: Kwan can occupy position 2 or 4 in this scenario (e.g., Fabre-1, Jenks-2, Gomez-3, Kwan-4, Ingram-5, Holt-6 or Jenks-1, Fabre-2, Gomez-3, Kwan-4, Ingram-5, Holt-6), but could also be elsewhere, so Kwan is not forced to fourth.
explanations.E: Correct — Rule 5 mandates Ingram at fifth whenever Gomez is third.

questions.questionStem: If Kwan finishes third, then which one of the following could be true?

explanations.correct: With Kwan at 3, Fabre must precede Gomez, and Jenks must precede Holt with Holt and Ingram adjacent. One valid arrangement: Fabre-1, Jenks-2, Kwan-3, Gomez-4, Holt-5, Ingram-6 — but Kwan cannot be sixth (satisfied) and Ingram-6 with Holt-5 is adjacent ✓. Checking Rule 5: Gomez is at 4, not 3, so the conditional does not fire ✓. Gomez finishing fourth is therefore possible.
explanations.A: With Kwan at 3, Jenks must finish before Holt (Rule 3), and Holt–Ingram must be adjacent (Rule 2). Jenks at 4 would force Holt to 5 or later; Ingram adjacent to Holt would be at 4 or 6. But Jenks at 4 means positions 1–2 must hold Fabre and one other from {Gomez, Holt, Ingram}, and Fabre must precede Gomez. In every arrangement with Jenks-4, Holt can only be 5 or 6; if Holt-5 then Ingram-4 or 6, but Jenks is at 4, so Ingram-6. But then Gomez must be after Fabre and must fit in positions 1, 2, or 6 — Gomez-6 is taken by Ingram. Fabre must be before Gomez, leaving no valid slot. No valid solution has Jenks fourth when Kwan is third.
explanations.B: Holt at 2 would require Jenks at 1 (Rule 3: Jenks before Holt). Ingram adjacent to Holt must be at 1 or 3, but Jenks is at 1 and Kwan is at 3, so no valid slot exists for Ingram. Impossible.
explanations.C: Ingram at 1: Rule 2 requires Holt adjacent, so Holt at 2. Rule 3 requires Jenks before Holt(2), so Jenks at 1 — but Ingram is at 1. Contradiction; impossible.
explanations.D: Fabre at 5 means Gomez must be at 6. Positions 1, 2, and 4 hold Jenks, Holt, and Ingram in some order with Jenks before Holt and Holt–Ingram adjacent. Jenks-1, Holt-2, Ingram-3 but Kwan is at 3 — no room. Jenks-1, Ingram-2, Holt-3 but Kwan is at 3 — no room. Jenks-2, Holt-4, Ingram-... Ingram must be adjacent to Holt(4), so Ingram at 3 or 5; Kwan at 3 and Fabre at 5, so no valid slot. Fabre cannot finish fifth when Kwan is third.
explanations.E: Correct — Gomez can finish fourth when Kwan is third (e.g., Fabre-1, Jenks-2, Kwan-3, Gomez-4, Holt-5, Ingram-6).
